summary.short: Amends four California Penal Code sections to cover child sexual-abuse matter that is digitally altered or AI-generated and depicts a person under 18. Applies to any person; operative only if AB 1831 is enacted and takes effect by January 1, 2025.
summary.long: SB 1381 amends four California Penal Code sections on child sexual-abuse material to cover matter that is digitally altered or generated by artificial intelligence. Section 311.1 (obscene matter depicting a person under 18) and Section 311.3 (sexual exploitation of a child) now reach such matter, including data depicting what appears to be a minor engaged in or simulating sexual conduct. Section 311.1 carries up to one year in county jail and a $1,000 fine, or state prison and a $10,000 fine. Section 311.3(e) carries a fine up to $2,000, up to one year in county jail, or both, with state prison after a prior conviction. Section 311.4 extends its minor-employment and minor-use offences to such matter; subdivision (b) is a felony with three, six or eight years in state prison where commercial purposes are shown. Section 312.3 adds such matter to the definition of matter subject to forfeiture and destruction. Existing exemptions for law enforcement, legitimate medical, scientific or educational activities, lawful conduct between spouses and legally emancipated minors are retained. Section 5 provides that no state reimbursement is required for local agencies. Section 6 makes the act operative only if AB 1831 of the 2023–24 Regular Session is enacted and takes effect on or before January 1, 2025.
